passages.title: 藍色幽靈號登陸月球
passages.text: On March 2, 2025, a spacecraft called Blue Ghost landed safely on the {1}. It was built by Firefly Aerospace, an American company. Other companies had tried before, but some of their landers crashed or fell over. Blue Ghost was the first lander from a private company to touch down standing up and finish all of its work. It carried ten science tools for NASA and worked on the surface for about two weeks. On March 14, it saw something special: the {2} moved in front of the sun and hid it for a while. That night, people on our {3} saw a red "blood moon," but Blue Ghost saw a solar eclipse from the other side. My science teacher showed us its photos in class. They showed a {4} ring of light in a black sky. She told us that the moon has no air, so its sky is dark even during the day. After that class, I {5} to learn more about space.

blanks.why: landed on the moon「降落在月球上」，這艘太空船是登月任務。pillow（枕頭）、wallet（皮夾）、cookie（餅乾）都不是太空船降落的地方。
the earth moved in front of the sun「地球移到太陽前面」，從月球上看，就是地球把太陽遮住，形成日食。spoon（湯匙）、drawer（抽屜）、candle（蠟燭）都不可能擋住太陽。
people on our planet「我們這顆星球上的人」，指地球上的人看到月食。sandwich（三明治）、sock（襪子）、eraser（橡皮擦）上面不會住著「人們」。
a bright ring of light「一圈明亮的光環」，bright 形容光很亮。lazy（懶惰的）、rude（無禮的）、patient（有耐心的）都是形容人的個性，不能形容光。
decided to learn「決定要學」，decide + to V。sneezed（打噴嚏）、coughed（咳嗽）、fried（油炸）都不能接 to learn 表示決定。

passages.zh: 2025 年 3 月 2 日，一艘名叫「藍色幽靈」的太空船平安降落在月球上。它是由美國的螢火蟲太空公司打造的。之前也有其他公司嘗試過，但有些登陸器墜毀或翻倒了。藍色幽靈是第一個由民間公司製造、站著平穩著陸並完成所有任務的登陸器。它幫美國太空總署載了十件科學儀器，在月球表面工作了大約兩個星期。3 月 14 日，它看到了特別的景象：地球移到太陽前面，把太陽遮住了一段時間。那天晚上，我們地球上的人看到紅色的「血月」，藍色幽靈則從另一邊看到了日食。自然老師在課堂上給我們看它拍的照片，照片裡是一圈明亮的光環，掛在黑色的天空中。她告訴我們，月球上沒有空氣，所以就算是白天，天空也是黑的。上完那堂課，我決定要多了解太空。

passages.title: 嫦娥六號帶回月球背面的土
passages.text: In June 2024, China's Chang'e-6 spacecraft brought back the first rocks and soil from the far side of the {1}. The moon always shows the same face to the {2}, so people on the ground can never see its far side. That also makes it {3} to talk to a lander there. China first sent a special satellite to pass messages back and forth. On June 2, Chang'e-6 landed inside a huge, old crater on the far side. It used a drill and a robot arm to collect samples. Then a small rocket carried them up to another spacecraft, which flew them home. On June 25, the capsule landed in Inner Mongolia with about 1,935 grams of samples. Scientists {4} that these rocks will tell us how the moon was formed. They may also help us understand the early history of our own {5}.

blanks.why: the far side of the moon「月球的背面」，嫦娥六號是到月球背面取樣。towel（毛巾）、button（鈕扣）、sofa（沙發）沒有「背面的岩石和土壤」可以帶回來。
shows the same face to the earth「總是用同一面對著地球」，所以地面上的人看不到月球背面。lamp（燈）、coin（硬幣）、belt（皮帶）都和「地面上的人看不到」無關。
makes it difficult to talk「使得通訊很困難」，make it + 形容詞 + to V。polite（有禮貌的）、lazy（懶惰的）、friendly（友善的）都是形容人的個性，不能說明「通訊」的狀況。
Scientists hope that…「科學家希望……」，hope 可以接 that 子句。cough、sneeze（打噴嚏）、bake（烘烤）都不能接 that 子句表示期望。
the early history of our own planet「我們自己這顆行星（地球）早期的歷史」。pocket（口袋）、bowl（碗）、scarf（圍巾）都沒有「早期歷史」可以研究。

passages.zh: 2024 年 6 月，中國的嫦娥六號太空船首次從月球背面帶回岩石和土壤。月球總是用同一面對著地球，所以地面上的人永遠看不到它的背面。這也讓和背面登陸器通訊變得很困難，所以中國先發射了一顆特別的衛星來來回回傳遞訊息。6 月 2 日，嫦娥六號降落在月球背面一個巨大而古老的隕石坑裡。它用鑽頭和機械手臂採集樣本，再由一枚小火箭把樣本送到另一艘太空船上，載回地球。6 月 25 日，返回艙帶著大約 1,935 公克的樣本降落在內蒙古。科學家希望這些岩石能告訴我們月球是怎麼形成的，也可能幫助我們了解我們自己這顆行星早期的歷史。

passages.title: 地球多了一個「迷你月亮」
passages.text: In the fall of 2024, the {1} had a second moon for a short time. Scientists called it a "mini-moon." It was a small space rock named 2024 PT5, and it was only about ten meters across. From September 29 to November 25, it moved slowly near our {2}, because the earth's pull was strong enough to hold it for a while. It never went all the way around us, though. After that, it went back to traveling around the sun. Many people wanted to see it, but it was too small and dark for our eyes. You needed a {3} telescope to see it at all. Some scientists think the rock may be a piece of the real {4} that broke off long ago, when something hit it. My classmate said our moon had a baby. Our teacher {5} at the joke. Then she told us that small visitors like this have come before, for example in 2006 and 2020.

blanks.why: the earth had a second moon「地球有了第二個月亮」。pumpkin（南瓜）、sock（襪子）、kettle（水壺）都不會有月亮繞著它。
moved near our planet「在我們的星球附近移動」，下一句說地球的引力抓住它。ladder（梯子）、tissue（面紙）、carpet（地毯）都和地球引力無關。
a special telescope「特別的（大型）望遠鏡」。hungry（餓的）、angry（生氣的）、lonely（寂寞的）都是形容人或動物的感受，不能形容望遠鏡。
a piece of the real moon「真正月球的一小塊」，科學家認為它可能是很久以前月球被撞擊時飛出的碎片。kettle、ladder、tissue 都不會「被東西撞到後掉出一塊」飛到太空中。
laughed at the joke「聽了笑話笑出來」，laugh at 是固定搭配。boiled（煮沸）、borrowed（借入）、painted（畫）都不能接 at the joke。

passages.zh: 2024 年秋天，地球短暫擁有了第二個月亮，科學家叫它「迷你月亮」。它是一顆名叫 2024 PT5 的小太空岩石，直徑只有大約十公尺。從 9 月 29 日到 11 月 25 日，它在我們的星球附近慢慢移動，因為地球的引力強到足以暫時抓住它。不過，它從來沒有完整繞地球一圈，之後又回去繞著太陽運行。很多人想看看它，但它太小又太暗，肉眼看不到，要用特別的望遠鏡才看得到。有些科學家認為，這顆岩石可能是很久以前月球被撞擊時掉下來的一小塊。我同學說我們的月亮生了一個寶寶，老師聽了這個笑話笑了出來，接著告訴我們，以前也有這樣的小訪客來過，例如 2006 年和 2020 年。

passages.title: 差點撞上地球的小行星
passages.text: In December 2024, a telescope in Chile found a space rock named 2024 YR4. It is about 60 meters wide. When scientists first worked out its path, they found that it might hit the {1} in December 2032. In February 2025, the chance went up to about 3 percent. The news spread fast, and people all over the {2} {3} about it. But more careful study soon showed that the rock would miss us. Then scientists said there was a small chance, about 4 percent, that it could hit the {4} instead. Many people even hoped to watch the crash with a telescope. {5}, after more study, scientists said it would miss the moon, too. My science teacher said this story shows why we keep watching the sky. It is much better to find a dangerous rock years before it comes close.

blanks.why: might hit the earth「可能撞上地球」，下一段說後來確定會「錯過我們」。pillow（枕頭）、cookie（餅乾）、scarf（圍巾）都不會被太空岩石撞上而引起全球擔心。
people all over the planet「全世界（全地球）的人」。bowl（碗）、sock（襪子）、button（鈕扣）上面不會有人。
worried about it「為這件事擔心」，worry about 是固定搭配。cooked（煮）、painted（畫）、sold（賣）都不能接 about it 表示擔心。
hit the moon instead「改成撞上月球」，下一句說後來確定也不會撞月球。blanket（毛毯）、wallet（皮夾）、spoon（湯匙）都不在太空中。
Later, after more study「後來，經過更多研究」，later 表示「之後」。ago 要放在時間後面（two years ago），below（在下面）、ever（曾經）都不能放在句首表示「後來」。

passages.zh: 2024 年 12 月，智利的一座望遠鏡發現了一顆名叫 2024 YR4 的太空岩石，它大約 60 公尺寬。科學家剛算出它的軌道時，發現它可能在 2032 年 12 月撞上地球。2025 年 2 月，這個機率上升到大約百分之三。消息傳得很快，全世界的人都為此擔心。但更仔細的研究很快證明，這顆岩石不會撞到我們。接著科學家說，它有大約百分之四的小機率會改撞月球，很多人甚至希望能用望遠鏡看到撞擊。後來，經過更多研究，科學家說它也不會撞上月球。自然老師說，這個故事告訴我們為什麼要一直觀察天空：在危險的岩石接近之前好幾年就發現它，會好得多。

passages.title: 土星又多了 128 個衛星
passages.text: In March 2025, a team of scientists said they had {1} 128 new {2} around Saturn. That brought Saturn's total to 274. It now has almost twice as many moons as all the other planets put together. The team was led by Dr. Edward Ashton, who was working at Academia Sinica in Taiwan at that time. Most of the new moons are only a few kilometers wide. Scientists think they are pieces of bigger moons that broke apart after crashes long ago. So Saturn is still the {3} with the most moons in our solar system. Jupiter comes second with 95. When I read this news on my phone, I felt {4} that part of the work was done in Taiwan. By the way, our own {5} has only one moon, but it is a big one!

blanks.why: had found 128 new moons「發現了 128 顆新衛星」，find 的過去分詞是 found。cooked（煮）、washed（洗）、borrowed（借）都不能用在「衛星」上。
128 new moons around Saturn「繞著土星的 128 顆新衛星」，moon 也可以指其他行星的衛星。spoons、socks、cookies 不會繞著土星轉。
the planet with the most moons「衛星最多的行星」，土星是行星。pillow（枕頭）、kettle（水壺）、ladder（梯子）不會有衛星。
felt proud that…「對……感到驕傲」，因為研究是在台灣完成的。thick（厚的）、salty（鹹的）、sour（酸的）都不能形容人的心情。
our own earth has only one moon「我們的地球只有一個月亮」。carpet（地毯）、tissue（面紙）、button（鈕扣）都不會有月亮。

passages.zh: 2025 年 3 月，一組科學家宣布他們在土星周圍發現了 128 顆新衛星，讓土星的衛星總數達到 274 顆，幾乎是其他所有行星加起來的兩倍。這個團隊由艾德華‧艾希頓博士帶領，他當時在台灣的中央研究院工作。大部分新衛星只有幾公里寬，科學家認為它們是很久以前較大的衛星撞擊碎裂後留下的碎片。所以土星仍然是太陽系裡衛星最多的行星，木星以 95 顆排第二。我在手機上讀到這則新聞時，對部分研究是在台灣完成的感到很驕傲。順帶一提，我們自己的地球只有一個月亮，不過是很大的一個！

passages.title: 飛向木衛二的歐羅巴快船
passages.text: On October 14, 2024, NASA sent the spacecraft Europa Clipper into space. It is the biggest spacecraft NASA has ever built to study another {1} or its moons. With its solar panels open, it is about 30 meters wide, longer than a basketball court. It is going to Europa, one of Jupiter's {2}. Europa is covered with ice, but scientists believe there is a huge, salty ocean under the ice. It may hold about twice as much water as all the oceans on {3}. Life needs water, so scientists want to know if Europa has the right {4} for living things. The trip is about 2.9 billion kilometers long, and Clipper will arrive in 2030. It will not land, but it will fly past Europa about 50 times. The spacecraft also carries a poem and the names of 2.6 million people. My cousin {5} her name, too, so part of her is flying to Jupiter!

blanks.why: another planet or its moons「另一顆行星或它的衛星」，木星是行星。pocket（口袋）、towel（毛巾）、cookie（餅乾）都不需要用太空船去研究。
one of Jupiter's moons「木星的衛星之一」，歐羅巴（木衛二）是木星的衛星。wallets、kettles、pillows 不會繞著木星轉。
all the oceans on earth「地球上所有的海洋」，拿來和歐羅巴的海洋比較。ladder（梯子）、carpet（地毯）、scarf（圍巾）上面沒有海洋。
the right environment for living things「適合生物的環境」。umbrella（雨傘）、eraser（橡皮擦）、sandwich（三明治）不是一顆衛星「有沒有」的生存條件。
sent her name「寄出她的名字」，send 的過去式是 sent。grew（種植；長大）、baked（烘烤）、slept（睡覺）都不能接 her name，也不能讓名字「飛向木星」。

passages.zh: 2024 年 10 月 14 日，美國太空總署把歐羅巴快船號送上太空。這是美國太空總署為了研究其他行星或它們的衛星，所打造過最大的太空船；太陽能板展開時大約 30 公尺寬，比一座籃球場還長。它要前往木星的衛星之一——歐羅巴。歐羅巴表面被冰覆蓋，但科學家相信冰層下有一片巨大的鹹水海洋，水量可能是地球上所有海洋的兩倍左右。生命需要水，所以科學家想知道歐羅巴有沒有適合生物的環境。這趟旅程大約 29 億公里，快船號會在 2030 年抵達。它不會降落，但會飛越歐羅巴大約 50 次。太空船上還載著一首詩和 260 萬人的名字。我表姊也寄了她的名字，所以她的一部分正飛向木星呢！

passages.title: 世界地球日的年度主題
passages.text: Earth Day is on April 22 every year. It started in the United States in 1970, and now people in more than 190 countries take part. Every year, the group EARTHDAY.ORG chooses a theme. The theme for 2024 was "Planet vs. Plastics." It asked people to use less plastic, because plastic {1} hurts sea animals and stays in nature for a very long time. The theme for 2025 was "Our Power, Our Planet." It asked people to use more clean power from the sun, wind, and water, because clean power is better for the whole {2}. This year, our class {3} Earth Day in a simple way. We turned off the lights and fans in our classroom for one hour. We also {4} our own cups to the drink shop after school. Our teacher said small actions like these can help protect the {5} when many people do them together.

blanks.why: plastic pollution「塑膠汙染」，傷害海洋動物、在大自然中很久都不會消失。pumpkin（南瓜）、blanket（毛毯）、tissue（面紙）都不能和 plastic 組成會傷害海洋動物的問題。
better for the whole planet「對整個地球更好」。bottle（瓶子）、ladder（梯子）、sofa（沙發）都不是「乾淨能源」要照顧的對象。
celebrated Earth Day「慶祝世界地球日」，celebrate + 節日。coughed（咳嗽）、sneezed（打噴嚏）、boiled（煮沸）都不能接 Earth Day 當受詞。
brought our own cups「帶自己的杯子」，bring 的過去式是 brought。smelled our own cups 意思不通，slept（睡覺）、cried（哭）不能接受詞。
protect the environment「保護環境」，是固定搭配。kettle（水壺）、button（鈕扣）、wallet（皮夾）都不是關燈、自備杯子要保護的東西。

passages.zh: 每年的 4 月 22 日是世界地球日。它在 1970 年從美國開始，現在有超過 190 個國家的人參與。每年，地球日組織都會選一個主題。2024 年的主題是「地球對抗塑膠」，請大家少用塑膠，因為塑膠汙染會傷害海洋動物，而且會在大自然裡留存很久很久。2025 年的主題是「我們的力量，我們的地球」，請大家多使用來自太陽、風和水的乾淨能源，因為乾淨能源對整個地球更好。今年，我們班用簡單的方式慶祝地球日：我們把教室的燈和電扇關掉一小時，放學後去飲料店時也自己帶杯子。老師說，當很多人一起做的時候，像這樣的小行動就能幫忙保護環境。

passages.title: 月球每年離我們遠一點
passages.text: Did you know that the {1} is {2} moving away from us? Every year, it moves about 3.8 centimeters farther from the {3}. That is about as fast as your fingernails grow. How do scientists know this? From 1969 to 1971, Apollo astronauts left special mirrors on the moon's surface. Since then, scientists on our {4} have shot laser light at these mirrors. They measure how long it takes for the light to {5}. The round trip takes about two and a half seconds. Why is the moon moving away? The moon's pull makes ocean tides on the earth, and the tides give the moon a tiny push every day. Don't worry, though. The moon will stay with us for a very, very long time. My little sister was happy to hear that. She said she still needs the moon for the Moon Festival every year!

blanks.why: the moon is moving away from us「月亮正在遠離我們」，下文說月亮每年遠離 3.8 公分。pumpkin（南瓜）、wallet（皮夾）、towel（毛巾）不會每年離地球遠一點。
slowly moving away「慢慢地遠離」，一年只移動 3.8 公分，所以是「慢慢地」。rudely（無禮地）、bravely（勇敢地）、politely（有禮貌地）都是形容人的態度，不能形容月球移動。
farther from the earth「離地球更遠」。blanket（毛毯）、button（鈕扣）、scarf（圍巾）都不是月球遠離的對象。
scientists on our planet「在我們星球上的科學家」，從地球發射雷射光到月球。cookie（餅乾）、sock（襪子）、kettle（水壺）上面不會有科學家。
for the light to return「光線返回」，光打到鏡子後反射回來。explore（探索）、decorate（裝飾）、imagine（想像）都不能用來描述光的來回。

passages.zh: 你知道月亮正在慢慢離我們而去嗎？它每年離地球大約遠 3.8 公分，差不多和指甲生長的速度一樣快。科學家怎麼知道的呢？1969 到 1971 年間，阿波羅計畫的太空人在月球表面留下了特殊的鏡子。從那時起，我們星球上的科學家就把雷射光打向這些鏡子，測量光線要多久才會返回，一趟來回大約兩秒半。月亮為什麼會遠離？月球的引力在地球上造成海洋潮汐，而潮汐每天都會輕輕推月球一下。不過別擔心，月亮還會陪我們非常非常久。我妹妹聽了很開心，她說她每年中秋節還需要月亮呢！

passages.title: 看不見銀河的城市
passages.text: Have you ever seen the Milky Way with your own eyes? Many of us never have. A study in 2016 found that about one third of the people on {1} cannot see the Milky Way from where they live. In North America, the number is almost 80 percent. The reason is light {2}. Street lights, signs, and tall buildings make the night sky too bright, so we cannot see the weak light of faraway stars. Light pollution is a problem for animals, too. For example, baby sea turtles move toward the brightest part of the sky, which is usually over the sea. City lights can send them the wrong way. Last summer, my family {3} to a mountain with no city lights around. After the {4} went down, the sky was full of stars. I could even see the {5} Jupiter shining like a bright star. It was the most beautiful night sky I have ever seen.

blanks.why: people on earth「地球上的人」。sofa（沙發）、tissue（面紙）、bottle（瓶子）上面不會住著全世界三分之一的人。
light pollution「光害（光汙染）」，下文說路燈、招牌讓夜空太亮。pillow（枕頭）、cookie（餅乾）、kettle（水壺）都不能和 light 組成讓人看不到星星的問題。
traveled to a mountain「到山上旅行」，travel to + 地點。coughed（咳嗽）、sneezed（打噴嚏）、boiled（煮沸）都不能接 to a mountain 表示去某地。
After the moon went down「月亮下山以後」，月光消失，星星就更清楚。ladder（梯子）、carpet（地毯）、button（鈕扣）不會在夜空中「落下」。
the planet Jupiter「木星這顆行星」。towel、wallet、scarf 都不能放在 Jupiter 前面說明它是什麼。

passages.zh: 你曾經親眼看過銀河嗎？我們很多人都沒看過。2016 年的一項研究發現，地球上大約三分之一的人在自己住的地方看不到銀河，在北美洲，這個比例將近百分之八十。原因是光害。路燈、招牌和高樓讓夜空太亮，我們就看不見遙遠星星微弱的光。光害對動物也是個問題，例如剛孵出來的小海龜會朝天空最亮的方向爬，而那通常是在海的上方，城市的燈光可能讓牠們走錯方向。去年夏天，我們全家去了一座附近沒有城市燈光的山上。月亮下山以後，滿天都是星星，我甚至看得到木星像一顆亮星一樣閃耀。那是我看過最美的夜空。

passages.title: 地球離太陽最近的時候是冬天
passages.text: Many people think summer is hot because the {1} is closer to the sun then. In fact, that is a myth. Every year, our {2} is closest to the sun in early January, which is winter in Taiwan! It is farthest from the sun in early July. The difference is about five million kilometers. So why is it hot in summer? It is hot in summer {3} the earth is tilted. From June to August, the northern half of the {4} leans toward the sun. Sunlight hits Taiwan more directly, and the days are longer, so it gets hot. At the same time, the southern half leans away from the sun, so it has winter. That is why the seasons in Australia are opposite to ours. My cousin lives in Sydney, and she {5} Christmas at the beach every year!

blanks.why: the earth is closer to the sun「地球離太陽比較近」。spoon（湯匙）、pillow（枕頭）、sock（襪子）跟季節冷熱無關，也不會「離太陽近」。
our planet is closest to the sun「我們的星球離太陽最近」，指地球。candle（蠟燭）、tissue（面紙）、cookie（餅乾）都不會繞太陽轉。
It is hot in summer because…「夏天熱是因為……」，because 說明原因。until（直到）、unless（除非）、whether（是否）都不能用來說明「為什麼熱」。
the northern half of the earth「地球的北半部（北半球）」。bowl（碗）、ladder（梯子）、wallet（皮夾）都沒有「北半部朝向太陽」的說法。
celebrates Christmas「過聖誕節」，主詞 she 是第三人稱單數，所以加 s。coughs（咳嗽）、sneezes（打噴嚏）、sleeps（睡覺）都不能接 Christmas 當受詞。

passages.zh: 很多人以為夏天很熱，是因為那時地球離太陽比較近。事實上，這是錯誤的說法。每年我們的星球在一月初離太陽最近，那時台灣是冬天！七月初則離太陽最遠，兩者相差大約五百萬公里。那麼夏天為什麼熱呢？夏天熱是因為地球是傾斜的。六月到八月，地球的北半部朝太陽傾斜，陽光比較直接照到台灣，白天也比較長，所以天氣變熱。同時，南半部背向太陽，所以那裡是冬天。這就是為什麼澳洲的季節和我們相反。我表姊住在雪梨，她每年都在海灘上過聖誕節！

passages.title: 太空站上其實有重力
passages.text: Many people think astronauts float on the International Space Station because there is no gravity in space. That is a myth. The station is only about 400 kilometers above the {1}, and gravity there is still about 90 percent as strong as on the ground. So why do astronauts float? It is because the station is falling around our {2} all the time. It {3} so fast, about 28,000 kilometers an hour, that it keeps missing the ground as it falls. The astronauts are falling with it, so they feel as if they have no weight. Gravity is everywhere in space. It {4} the moon going around the earth, and it keeps the earth going around the sun. On the {5}, gravity is only about one sixth as strong as on the earth. That is why the Apollo astronauts could jump so easily there.

blanks.why: 400 kilometers above the earth「在地球上方 400 公里」。eraser（橡皮擦）、kettle（水壺）、scarf（圍巾）都不能當作太空站高度的參考點。
falling around our planet「一直繞著我們的星球掉落」，也就是繞地球運行。pocket（口袋）、cookie（餅乾）、towel（毛巾）都不是太空站繞行的對象。
It moves so fast「它移動得非常快」，主詞 it 是單數，所以用 moves。sleeps（睡覺）、smiles（微笑）、smells（聞起來）都不能用來說明太空站「多快」，so fast 要搭配表示移動的動詞。
keeps the moon going around「讓月亮持續繞著轉」，keep + 受詞 + V-ing。borrows（借）、paints（畫）、washes（洗）都沒有「使……持續」的用法。
On the moon, gravity is one sixth…「在月球上，重力只有六分之一」，所以阿波羅太空人跳得很輕鬆。sofa（沙發）、pillow（枕頭）、wallet（皮夾）上面不是太空人跳躍的地方。

passages.zh: 很多人以為太空人在國際太空站裡會漂浮，是因為太空中沒有重力。這是錯誤的說法。太空站只在地球上方大約 400 公里，那裡的重力仍然有地面的百分之九十左右。那太空人為什麼會漂浮？因為太空站一直繞著我們的星球「掉落」。它移動得非常快，時速大約 28,000 公里，所以一邊掉落，一邊不斷錯過地面。太空人和太空站一起掉落，所以感覺好像沒有重量。重力在太空中無所不在，它讓月亮持續繞著地球轉，也讓地球持續繞著太陽轉。在月球上，重力只有地球的六分之一左右，這就是阿波羅太空人在那裡能輕鬆跳躍的原因。

passages.title: 冥王星為什麼不是行星了
passages.text: When my dad was in school, he learned that there were nine {1} in our solar system. Today, we learn that there are eight. What happened? Pluto was {2} in 1930 by Clyde Tombaugh, a young American. For 76 years, it was called the ninth planet. But later, scientists found many other icy objects near Pluto, and one of them, Eris, is about the same size as Pluto. In 2006, a group of scientists from around the world {3} on a new meaning of "planet." A planet must go around the sun, be round, and clear its path of other big objects. Pluto shares its path with many icy objects, so it became a "dwarf {4}." Pluto is even smaller than our {5}! But it is still an interesting place. It has five moons of its own, and its biggest moon, Charon, is about half as wide as Pluto.

blanks.why: nine planets in our solar system「太陽系的九大行星」。spoons、socks、pillows 都不是太陽系的成員。
Pluto was found in 1930「冥王星在 1930 年被發現」，被動語態 was + 過去分詞 found。cried、laughed、swam 都不能放在 was 後面形成被動語態。
decided on a new meaning「決定了新的定義」，decide on 表示「決定、選定」。cooked（煮）、swept（掃）、smelled（聞）都不能接 on a new meaning。
a dwarf planet「矮行星」，冥王星被改列為矮行星。ruler（尺）、eraser（橡皮擦）、wallet（皮夾）和 dwarf 組合起來都不是天體的類別。
smaller than our moon「比我們的月亮還小」。towel（毛巾）、kettle（水壺）、carpet（地毯）拿來和冥王星比大小都不合理。

passages.zh: 我爸爸讀書的時候，學到太陽系有九大行星；現在我們學到的是八大行星。發生了什麼事？冥王星是在 1930 年由一位年輕的美國人湯博發現的，之後 76 年它都被稱為第九顆行星。但後來，科學家在冥王星附近找到許多其他冰冷的天體，其中一顆鬩神星和冥王星差不多大。2006 年，來自世界各地的科學家決定了「行星」的新定義：行星必須繞著太陽轉、形狀是圓的，而且要清空軌道上其他大型天體。冥王星和許多冰冷天體共用軌道，所以變成了「矮行星」。冥王星甚至比我們的月亮還小！但它仍是個有趣的地方。它自己有五顆衛星，最大的凱倫寬度大約是冥王星的一半。

passages.title: 從月球拍到的「地出」
passages.text: On December 24, 1968, three astronauts on Apollo 8 became the first people to fly around the {1}. As their spacecraft came around the moon, astronaut Bill Anders saw the {2} rising above the moon's gray surface. He quickly took a color photo. The photo, later called "Earthrise," shows our blue and white {3} alone in black space. Many people say the picture made them see how small and special the earth is. Less than two years later, on April 22, 1970, about 20 million Americans joined the first Earth Day to protect the {4}. Today, Earthrise is one of the most famous photos ever taken. Last week, our art teacher showed it to us and asked us to {5} the earth from space. I painted it as a small blue ball, just like the one in the photo.

blanks.why: fly around the moon「繞月飛行」，阿波羅 8 號是第一次載人繞月。pocket（口袋）、eraser（橡皮擦）、candle（蠟燭）都不是太空船繞行的地方。
saw the earth rising「看到地球升起」，這張照片就叫「地出」。scarf（圍巾）、bowl（碗）、sock（襪子）不會從月球表面「升起」。
our blue and white planet「我們藍白相間的星球」，指照片中的地球。blanket（毛毯）、cookie（餅乾）、ruler（尺）不會孤單地掛在黑色太空中。
protect the environment「保護環境」，地球日的目的。umbrella（雨傘）、pillow（枕頭）、towel（毛巾）不需要兩千萬人一起保護。
asked us to draw the earth「要我們畫地球」，ask + 人 + to V；美術課畫畫。sleep（睡覺）、cry（哭）、sneeze（打噴嚏）都不能接 the earth 當受詞。

passages.zh: 1968 年 12 月 24 日，阿波羅 8 號上的三位太空人成為第一批繞月飛行的人。當太空船繞過月球時，太空人比爾‧安德斯看到地球從灰色的月球表面上升起，他很快拍下一張彩色照片。這張後來被稱為「地出」的照片，拍下我們藍白相間的星球孤單地掛在黑色太空中。許多人說，這張照片讓他們看到地球有多麼渺小又特別。不到兩年後的 1970 年 4 月 22 日，大約兩千萬美國人參加了第一屆世界地球日，一起保護環境。今天，「地出」是史上最有名的照片之一。上星期，美術老師給我們看這張照片，要我們畫出從太空看到的地球。我把它畫成一顆小小的藍色球，就和照片裡的一樣。

passages.title: 比水星還大的衛星
passages.text: Which is bigger, a moon or a planet? Usually, it is the {1}. But Ganymede, one of Jupiter's {2}, is bigger than Mercury, the smallest planet in our solar system. Ganymede is more than 5,000 kilometers wide. It is the largest moon in the solar system. It is much bigger than our own {3}, and {4} bigger than Mercury. However, it is not heavier. Mercury is made mostly of rock and metal, but Ganymede has a lot of ice, so Mercury weighs about twice as much. Ganymede is also the only moon we know of that has its own magnetic field. Scientists think there is a salty ocean under its ice. Galileo first saw it through a telescope in 1610. In 2023, Europe {5} a spacecraft called JUICE to study Ganymede and other moons of Jupiter. It should reach Jupiter in 2031.

blanks.why: Usually, it is the planet「通常是行星比較大」。sandwich（三明治）、pillow（枕頭）、button（鈕扣）都不是題目問的「衛星或行星」之一。
one of Jupiter's moons「木星的衛星之一」，甘尼米德（木衛三）是木星的衛星。socks、kettles、wallets 不會繞著木星轉。
bigger than our own moon「比我們自己的月亮大」。ladder（梯子）、towel（毛巾）、carpet（地毯）都不是拿來和衛星比大小的天體。
even bigger than Mercury「甚至比水星還大」，even 加強比較級。ago 要放在時間後面，below（在下面）、across（橫越）都不能修飾 bigger。
sent a spacecraft「發射（送出）太空船」，send 的過去式是 sent。baked（烘烤）、swept（掃）、boiled（煮沸）都不能接 a spacecraft。

passages.zh: 衛星和行星，哪一個比較大？通常是行星。但木星的衛星之一甘尼米德，比太陽系中最小的行星水星還大。甘尼米德寬五千多公里，是太陽系最大的衛星，比我們的月亮大得多，甚至比水星還大。不過，它並沒有比較重。水星主要由岩石和金屬構成，甘尼米德卻有很多冰，所以水星的重量大約是它的兩倍。甘尼米德也是目前已知唯一擁有自己磁場的衛星，科學家認為它的冰層下有一片鹹水海洋。伽利略在 1610 年第一次用望遠鏡看到它。2023 年，歐洲發射了名叫 JUICE 的太空船，去研究甘尼米德和木星的其他衛星，預計 2031 年抵達木星。

passages.title: 在月球上打高爾夫
passages.text: On February 6, 1971, astronaut Alan Shepard did something no one had ever done before: he played golf on the {1}. Ten years earlier, Shepard had become the first American in space. In 1971, he flew to the moon on Apollo 14. Before the trip, he secretly had a golf club head made that could fit onto a tool for picking up moon rocks. At the end of his last moonwalk, he dropped two golf balls and {2} them with one hand. His thick space suit made it {3} to swing with both hands. He joked that the ball went for miles. Many years later, people studied the photos and found that the farther ball went only about 40 yards, or about 37 meters. Still, people on {4} watched the moment on TV. It was the first time anyone played a sport anywhere except our own {5}. Today, the golf club is kept in a museum.

blanks.why: played golf on the moon「在月球上打高爾夫球」，他是阿波羅 14 號登月的太空人。bottle（瓶子）、tissue（面紙）、scarf（圍巾）上面不能打高爾夫。
hit them with one hand「用一隻手擊球」，hit 的過去式還是 hit。baked（烘烤）、boiled（煮沸）、fried（油炸）不是打高爾夫的動作。
made it hard to swing「讓揮桿很困難」，make it + 形容詞 + to V。hungry（餓的）、lonely（寂寞的）、thirsty（口渴的）都是人的感受，不能形容「揮桿」這件事。
people on earth watched it on TV「地球上的人從電視上看到」。pocket（口袋）、drawer（抽屜）、kettle（水壺）上面不會有人看電視。
anywhere except our own planet「在我們自己的星球以外的地方」，指地球以外。towel（毛巾）、button（鈕扣）、pillow（枕頭）都不能和「在別的地方運動」做對比。

passages.zh: 1971 年 2 月 6 日，太空人艾倫‧雪帕德做了一件前所未有的事：他在月球上打高爾夫球。十年前，雪帕德成為第一個上太空的美國人；1971 年，他搭阿波羅 14 號飛往月球。出發前，他偷偷請人做了一個高爾夫球桿頭，可以裝在撿月球岩石用的工具上。在最後一次月球漫步快結束時，他丟下兩顆高爾夫球，用一隻手擊球，因為厚重的太空衣讓他很難用雙手揮桿。他開玩笑說球飛了好幾英里遠。許多年後，有人研究照片，發現飛得比較遠的那顆球只飛了大約 40 碼，也就是大約 37 公尺。即使如此，地球上的人都從電視上看到了這一刻。這是人類第一次在地球以外的地方從事運動。如今，那支球桿被保存在博物館裡。

passages.title: 用舊手機做的奧運獎牌
passages.text: For the Tokyo 2020 Olympics and Paralympics, Japan made about 5,000 medals in a very special way. From 2017 to 2019, people across Japan gave away their old phones and other small electronics. Japan {1} about 79,000 tonnes of them, including more than six million used phones. Workers took out the tiny bits of gold, silver, and copper inside, and used the metal to make every gold, silver, and bronze medal. This was good for the {2}. Old electronics often end up as {3} in the trash. If they are not handled well, they can cause {4} in the soil and water. Many athletes said the medals felt even more meaningful because so many people helped make them. The project also sent a message to people all over the {5}: old things can become treasures.

blanks.why: Japan collected about 79,000 tonnes「日本收集了大約七萬九千公噸（舊電子產品）」。laughed（笑）、sneezed（打噴嚏）、cried（哭）都不能直接接受詞「七萬九千公噸」。
good for the environment「對環境有好處」，回收舊手機可以減少廢棄物。pumpkin（南瓜）、eraser（橡皮擦）、blanket（毛毯）都不是回收行動要照顧的對象。
end up as waste in the trash「最後變成垃圾桶裡的廢棄物」。joy（喜悅）、fault（過錯）、talent（天分）都不會被丟進垃圾桶裡。
cause pollution in the soil and water「造成土壤和水的汙染」。pillow（枕頭）、spoon（湯匙）、kettle（水壺）都不是「沒處理好」會在土壤和水中造成的問題。
people all over the planet「全世界的人」。towel（毛巾）、wallet（皮夾）、ladder（梯子）上面不會有人。

gloss: 帕拉林匹克運動會（帕運）
passages.zh: 為了 2020 年東京奧運和帕運，日本用一種很特別的方式做了大約五千面獎牌。從 2017 到 2019 年，日本各地的人捐出了舊手機和其他小型電子產品。日本收集了大約七萬九千公噸，其中包括六百多萬支舊手機。工作人員把裡面一點一點的金、銀和銅取出來，用這些金屬做出每一面金牌、銀牌和銅牌。這對環境很有好處。舊電子產品常常最後變成垃圾桶裡的廢棄物，如果沒有好好處理，就可能汙染土壤和水。許多運動員說，因為有這麼多人一起幫忙，這些獎牌感覺更有意義。這個計畫也向全世界的人傳達了一個訊息：舊東西也可以變成寶物。

passages.title: 全世界最環保的足球隊
passages.text: Forest Green Rovers is a small football club in Nailsworth, a town in England. In 2010, businessman Dale Vince became its {1}. He wanted to make it the greenest football club in the world. Since 2015, the club has sold only vegan food at its stadium, because raising animals for meat is hard on the {2}. The grass on the field is cut by a robot mower that uses solar power. The club also collects rainwater to water the grass. Its electricity comes from the sun and the wind, which causes much less {3} than burning coal. In 2018, the United Nations named it the first football club to reach carbon neutral. My coach showed us a video about the club. He said a football team can be good on the field and good for the {4} too. Now our team brings water bottles instead of buying drinks, because we want to help the {5} in our own small way.

blanks.why: became its owner「成為它的老闆（擁有者）」。pumpkin（南瓜）、receipt（收據）、cough（咳嗽）都不能當一個人的身分。
hard on the environment「對環境造成負擔」，be hard on 表示「對……不好」。umbrella（雨傘）、pillow（枕頭）、eraser（橡皮擦）和「養動物吃肉」沒有關係。
much less pollution than burning coal「比燒煤少很多汙染」。blanket（毛毯）、cookie（餅乾）、ladder（梯子）都不是燒煤會產生的東西。
good for the planet「對地球好」，和 good on the field（在球場上表現好）對照。sandwich（三明治）、sock（襪子）、kettle（水壺）不是環保行動要照顧的對象。
help the earth「幫助地球」，自備水壺是愛地球的小行動。towel（毛巾）、candle（蠟燭）、wallet（皮夾）都不會因為少買飲料而得到幫助。

passages.zh: 森林綠流浪者隊是英格蘭小鎮奈爾斯沃斯的一支小型足球俱樂部。2010 年，商人戴爾‧文斯成為它的老闆，他想把它打造成世界上最環保的足球俱樂部。從 2015 年起，球場只賣純素食物，因為養動物吃肉會對環境造成負擔。球場的草由使用太陽能的割草機器人修剪，俱樂部也收集雨水來澆草。它的電來自太陽和風，比燒煤產生的汙染少很多。2018 年，聯合國認定它是第一個達到碳中和的足球俱樂部。我們教練給我們看一段介紹這支球隊的影片。他說一支足球隊可以在球場上表現好，也可以對地球好。現在我們球隊都自己帶水壺，不再買飲料，因為我們想用自己的小方法幫助地球。

passages.title: 邊跑步邊撿垃圾
passages.text: In 2016, a Swedish man named Erik Ahlström started a new kind of exercise in Stockholm. While he was running, he {1} a lot of trash on the streets, so he began to pick it up. People call this idea "plogging." The word comes from the Swedish words for "pick up" and the English word "jogging." Plogging soon became popular and spread to many countries. It is good for your body, because you bend down, stand up, and carry bags while you run. It is good for the {2} too, because it reduces {3} in parks and on beaches. Last Sunday, our school running club tried plogging along the river. In one hour, we {4} six big bags with bottles, cans, and plastic bags. My legs were tired, but I felt great. It was a fun way to exercise and take care of our {5} at the same time.

blanks.why: noticed a lot of trash「注意到很多垃圾」，notice 是及物動詞，直接接受詞。laughed（笑）、swam（游泳）、cried（哭）都不能直接接 a lot of trash 當受詞。
good for the earth「對地球好」。cookie（餅乾）、button（鈕扣）、sofa（沙發）都不會因為撿垃圾而變好。
reduces pollution in parks「減少公園裡的汙染」。pillow（枕頭）、towel（毛巾）、candle（蠟燭）都不是撿垃圾要減少的東西。
filled six big bags with…「用……裝滿六大袋」，fill A with B 是固定用法。cried、slept、smiled 都不能接受詞 six big bags。
take care of our planet「照顧我們的地球」。scarf（圍巾）、kettle（水壺）、wallet（皮夾）都不是撿垃圾要照顧的對象。

passages.zh: 2016 年，一位名叫艾瑞克‧阿斯壯的瑞典人在斯德哥爾摩開始了一種新的運動。他跑步時注意到街上有很多垃圾，就開始把垃圾撿起來。大家把這個點子叫做「撿跑」，這個字來自瑞典語的「撿起來」和英文的「慢跑」。撿跑很快就流行起來，傳到了許多國家。它對身體很好，因為跑步時要彎腰、站起來，還要提袋子；它對地球也很好，因為能減少公園和海灘上的汙染。上星期天，我們學校的路跑社沿著河邊試了撿跑。一小時內，我們用瓶子、罐子和塑膠袋裝滿了六大袋。我的腿很痠，但心情很好。這是一個一邊運動、一邊照顧地球的有趣方式。

passages.title: 電動方程式賽車
passages.text: Formula E is a car racing series for electric cars. Its first race was held on the streets of Beijing on September 13, 2014. Electric race cars do not burn gas, so they cause much less air {1} than normal race cars. They are also much quieter, so most races can be held on city streets, close to fans. Formula E wants to show that electric cars can be {2} and good for the {3} at the same time. Today's cars can go faster than 320 kilometers an hour. They can also get back some {4} when they slow down. In fact, about 40 percent of the power used in a race comes from braking. My uncle loves car racing, and he watched a Formula E race on TV with me. He said the cars sound like spaceships. I hope that one day, all cars will be electric, and our {5} will have cleaner air.

blanks.why: air pollution「空氣汙染」，電動車不燒汽油。sofa（沙發）、eraser（橡皮擦）、cookie（餅乾）都不能和 air 組成燒汽油造成的問題。
can be fast「可以很快」，下文說時速超過 320 公里。lonely（寂寞的）、polite（有禮貌的）、shy（害羞的）都是形容人，不能形容車子。
good for the environment「對環境好」。pocket（口袋）、candle（蠟燭）、bowl（碗）都不是電動車要照顧的對象。
get back some energy「回收一些能量」，下一句說比賽用的電有四成來自煞車。homework（作業）、habit（習慣）、grade（成績）不能在車子減速時「拿回來」。
our planet will have cleaner air「我們的地球會有更乾淨的空氣」。wallet（皮夾）、ladder（梯子）、scarf（圍巾）都不會「有空氣」。

passages.zh: 電動方程式賽車是專為電動車舉辦的賽車系列賽。它的第一場比賽在 2014 年 9 月 13 日於北京的街道上舉行。電動賽車不燒汽油，所以造成的空氣汙染比一般賽車少很多。它們也安靜得多，所以大部分比賽可以在市區街道上舉行，離車迷很近。電動方程式想證明電動車可以既快速又對環境友善。現在的賽車時速可以超過 320 公里，減速時還能回收一些能量；事實上，比賽中使用的電力大約有四成來自煞車。我叔叔很愛賽車，他和我一起看了一場電動方程式的電視轉播。他說這些車的聲音聽起來像太空船。我希望有一天所有車子都是電動的，我們的地球就會有更乾淨的空氣。

passages.title: 塞納河終於可以游泳了
passages.text: For more than 100 years, swimming in the Seine River in Paris was not allowed, mostly because of water {1}. Before the 2024 Olympics, Paris spent about 1.4 billion euros to clean the river. It was not easy. After heavy rain, the water became dirty again, and the men's triathlon had to be moved from July 30 to July 31. On July 31, the triathletes finally swam in the Seine. Cassandre Beaugrand of France {2} the women's gold medal, and Alex Yee of Great Britain won the men's. A year later, on July 5, 2025, three swimming areas in the river opened to the public. Many Parisians {3} and jumped into the water. People hope a cleaner river will make a better {4} for both fish and people. Paris also showed people around the {5} that even a dirty river can become clean again.

blanks.why: because of water pollution「因為水汙染」，所以塞納河一百多年來禁止游泳。pumpkin（南瓜）、blanket（毛毯）、wallet（皮夾）都不能和 water 組成禁止游泳的原因。
won the women's gold medal「贏得女子組金牌」，win 的過去式是 won。cried（哭）、slept（睡覺）、coughed（咳嗽）都不能接 the gold medal 當受詞。
cheered and jumped into the water「歡呼並跳進水裡」。borrowed（借）、boiled（煮沸）、painted（畫）都是及物動詞，後面少了受詞，句子不通。
a better environment for fish and people「對魚和人都更好的環境」。pillow（枕頭）、spoon（湯匙）、eraser（橡皮擦）不是河流乾淨後能帶給魚和人的東西。
people around the planet「全世界的人」。cookie（餅乾）、towel（毛巾）、kettle（水壺）上面不會有人。

passages.zh: 一百多年來，巴黎的塞納河禁止游泳，主要是因為水汙染。2024 年奧運之前，巴黎花了大約 14 億歐元清理河川，但並不容易：大雨過後河水又變髒，男子鐵人三項只好從 7 月 30 日延到 7 月 31 日。7 月 31 日，鐵人三項選手終於在塞納河裡游泳。法國的卡珊卓‧波格朗贏得女子組金牌，英國的亞歷克斯‧易則贏得男子組金牌。一年後的 2025 年 7 月 5 日，河上三個游泳區對民眾開放，許多巴黎人歡呼著跳進水裡。大家希望更乾淨的河流能為魚和人帶來更好的環境。巴黎也讓全世界的人看到，就算是骯髒的河流也能重新變乾淨。

passages.title: 種樹的諾貝爾和平獎得主馬塔伊
passages.text: Wangari Maathai was born in Kenya in 1940. She studied science in the United States and later became the first woman in East and Central Africa to earn a doctorate. Back in Kenya, she saw that many forests had been cut down. Women had to walk farther and farther to find firewood and clean water. In 1977, she started the Green Belt Movement. She {1} women how to grow young trees, and the group paid them a little money for each tree that lived. Over the years, the movement helped people {2} tens of millions of trees across Kenya. In 2004, Maathai became the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize. The prize was for her work for the {3}, democracy, and peace. She believed that taking care of the {4} and taking care of people go together. She died in 2011, but her trees are still growing. Her story shows that one person can start something that makes our {5} greener.

blanks.why: taught women how to grow trees「教婦女怎麼種樹」，teach 的過去式是 taught，teach + 人 + how to V。tasted（嚐）、swept（掃）、boiled（煮沸）都不能接「人 + how to V」。
helped people plant trees「幫助人們種樹」，help + 人 + 原形動詞。sneeze、cough、laugh 都不能接 trees 當受詞。
her work for the environment「她為環境所做的努力」，種樹就是保護環境。pillow（枕頭）、sandwich（三明治）、candle（蠟燭）和民主、和平並列都不合理。
taking care of the earth「照顧地球」，和照顧人並列。towel（毛巾）、button（鈕扣）、kettle（水壺）都不是她想保護的對象。
makes our planet greener「讓我們的地球更綠」。sock（襪子）、cookie（餅乾）、wallet（皮夾）都不會因為種樹而變綠。

passages.zh: 旺加里‧馬塔伊 1940 年出生於肯亞。她到美國讀科學，後來成為東非和中非第一位取得博士學位的女性。回到肯亞後，她看到許多森林被砍光，婦女必須走得越來越遠才能找到柴火和乾淨的水。1977 年，她發起了綠帶運動。她教婦女怎麼種小樹苗，每種活一棵樹，組織就付給她們一點錢。多年來，這個運動幫助人們在肯亞各地種下了數千萬棵樹。2004 年，馬塔伊成為第一位獲得諾貝爾和平獎的非洲女性，得獎是因為她為環境、民主與和平所做的努力。她相信照顧地球和照顧人是分不開的。她在 2011 年過世，但她種的樹還在生長。她的故事告訴我們，一個人也能開始做一件讓地球更綠的事。

passages.title: 把塑膠袋變成錢包的伊薩圖
passages.text: Isatou Ceesay grew up in Njau, a small {1} in The Gambia, a country in West Africa. When she was young, plastic bags began to appear everywhere in her town. People threw them away on the roads and in the fields. Some animals ate the bags and got sick. When people burned the bags, the smoke caused air {2}. In 1997, Ceesay and a small group of women had an idea. They washed the old bags, cut them into thin strips, and used them like yarn to make purses. Then they {3} the purses at markets. The women earned money for their families, and their town became cleaner. Later, the group grew, and they recycled thousands of bags every month. People now call Ceesay "the Queen of Recycling." Her story has been written into a children's book called One Plastic Bag. Our English teacher read it to us. She said we don't need to be rich or famous to help the {4}. We can all do something for the {5}.

blanks.why: a small village in The Gambia「甘比亞的一個小村莊」。spoon（湯匙）、cough（咳嗽）、receipt（收據）都不能當作一個人長大的地方。
the smoke caused air pollution「煙造成空氣汙染」。pumpkin（南瓜）、blanket（毛毯）、scarf（圍巾）都不能和 air 組成燒塑膠的後果。
sold the purses at markets「在市場賣錢包」，所以下一句說婦女賺到錢。cried（哭）、slept（睡覺）、laughed（笑）都不能直接接 the purses 當受詞。
help the environment「幫助環境」，回收塑膠袋就是保護環境。towel（毛巾）、candle（蠟燭）、button（鈕扣）都不是回收行動要幫助的對象。
do something for the earth「為地球做點事」。cookie（餅乾）、pillow（枕頭）、kettle（水壺）都不合句意。

passages.zh: 伊薩圖‧希賽在西非國家甘比亞的一個小村莊恩加烏長大。她小時候，塑膠袋開始在鎮上到處出現，人們把它們丟在路上和田裡，有些動物吃了塑膠袋就生病了。人們燒塑膠袋時，冒出的煙還造成空氣汙染。1997 年，希賽和幾位婦女想到一個點子：她們把舊塑膠袋洗乾淨、剪成細長條，當作毛線來編織錢包，再拿到市場去賣。婦女們為家人賺到錢，鎮上也變乾淨了。後來這個團體越來越大，每個月回收好幾千個塑膠袋。現在大家稱希賽為「回收女王」。她的故事被寫成一本童書《一個塑膠袋》，我們的英文老師唸給我們聽。老師說，我們不需要有錢或有名才能幫助環境，每個人都可以為地球做點事。

passages.title: 庫克：「我以身為同志為傲」
passages.text: Tim Cook has been the CEO of Apple since 2011. In October 2014, he wrote an article for the magazine Bloomberg Businessweek. In it, he told the world that he is gay. He wrote, "I'm proud to be gay." He {1} to speak in public because he hoped his story could help young people who feel {2} or are bullied for who they are. He became one of the first openly gay leaders of a big American company. Under his leadership, Apple has also worked to protect the {3}. In 2020, the company set a goal: by 2030, all of its products should be carbon neutral. This means making and using an Apple product should add almost no extra carbon to the air. Today, Apple uses more recycled metal in its phones and computers, so less needs to be dug out of the {4}. My friend said it is cool that a person can be honest about who he is and help the {5} at the same time.

blanks.why: decided to speak in public「決定公開說出來」，decide + to V。baked（烘烤）、swept（掃）、boiled（煮沸）都不能接 to speak。
young people who feel alone「感到孤單的年輕人」，feel + 形容詞。salty（鹹的）、thick（厚的）、cheap（便宜的）都不能形容人的感受。
protect the environment「保護環境」，下文說產品要達到碳中和。pumpkin（南瓜）、eraser（橡皮擦）、bottle（瓶子）都不是公司環保目標要保護的對象。
dug out of the earth「從地底挖出來」，金屬礦產來自地下。towel（毛巾）、sock（襪子）、candle（蠟燭）裡挖不出金屬。
help the planet「幫助地球」，指 Apple 的環保行動。wallet（皮夾）、cookie（餅乾）、ladder（梯子）都不合句意。

passages.zh: 提姆‧庫克從 2011 年起擔任蘋果公司執行長。2014 年 10 月，他為《彭博商業週刊》寫了一篇文章，在文中向全世界說出自己是同志。他寫道：「我以身為同志為傲。」他決定公開說出來，是因為希望自己的故事能幫助那些感到孤單、或因為做自己而被霸凌的年輕人。他成為最早公開出櫃的美國大公司領導人之一。在他的領導下，蘋果也努力保護環境。2020 年，公司訂下目標：到 2030 年，所有產品都要達到碳中和，也就是製造和使用一項蘋果產品，幾乎不會讓空氣中多出額外的碳。現在蘋果在手機和電腦裡使用更多回收金屬，就不需要從地底挖出那麼多新的金屬。我朋友說，一個人能誠實面對自己是誰，同時又幫助地球，真的很酷。

passages.title: 第一位非裔女太空人梅‧傑米森
passages.text: Mae Jemison grew up in Chicago. As a child, she loved science and {1}. She watched the Apollo {2} landings on TV and dreamed of going to space one day. She studied hard and became a doctor. She also worked as a doctor in Sierra Leone and Liberia in West Africa. In 1987, NASA {3} her as an astronaut. On September 12, 1992, she flew into space on the space shuttle Endeavour and became the first African American woman in space. During the eight-day trip, the shuttle went around the {4} 127 times. She did science experiments in space, and she looked down at our beautiful {5} from the window. After she left NASA, she started a science camp for students called The Earth We Share. She wants young people, especially girls, to know that science is for everyone.

blanks.why: loved science and dance「喜愛科學和舞蹈」，dance 在這裡是名詞。cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）、receipt（收據）都不是小孩會喜愛的興趣。
the Apollo moon landings「阿波羅登月」。spoon（湯匙）、pillow（枕頭）、scarf（圍巾）不能和 landings 組成太空任務。
NASA chose her as an astronaut「美國太空總署選她當太空人」，choose 的過去式是 chose。cooked（煮）、swept（掃）、boiled（煮沸）都不能接 her as an astronaut。
went around the earth 127 times「繞地球 127 圈」。towel（毛巾）、cookie（餅乾）、wallet（皮夾）都不是太空梭繞行的對象。
looked down at our beautiful planet「往下看我們美麗的星球」，指從太空看地球。bottle（瓶子）、sock（襪子）、candle（蠟燭）都不是從太空往下看到的東西。

passages.zh: 梅‧傑米森在芝加哥長大，小時候喜愛科學和舞蹈。她在電視上看阿波羅登月，夢想有一天能上太空。她努力讀書，成為一名醫生，還曾在西非的獅子山和賴比瑞亞擔任醫生。1987 年，美國太空總署選她成為太空人。1992 年 9 月 12 日，她搭乘奮進號太空梭飛上太空，成為第一位上太空的非裔美國女性。在八天的旅程中，太空梭繞地球 127 圈。她在太空中做科學實驗，也從窗戶往下看我們美麗的星球。離開太空總署後，她為學生創辦了一個名叫「我們共享的地球」的科學營。她希望年輕人，特別是女孩們，知道科學是屬於每個人的。

passages.title: BLACKPINK 為氣候發聲
passages.text: BLACKPINK is one of the most {1} girl groups in the world. In February 2021, the four members, Jisoo, Jennie, Rosé, and Lisa, were named advocates for COP26. COP26 was a big United Nations meeting about climate change, held in Glasgow, Scotland, that November. As advocates, BLACKPINK made videos to ask their fans to learn about climate change and take action to protect the {2}. During the meeting, they also sent a video message asking world leaders to act quickly to save our {3}. Many fans around the world shared the videos online. In November 2023, the members {4} honorary MBEs from King Charles III in London for their work as COP26 advocates. My friend Amy is a big BLINK. After watching their climate video, she started to turn off the lights when she leaves a room. She says she wants to do her part for the {5}, just like her favorite group.

blanks.why: one of the most popular girl groups「最受歡迎的女團之一」。sore（痠痛的）、thirsty（口渴的）、dizzy（頭暈的）都不能用來形容一個團體受不受歡迎。
protect the environment「保護環境」。umbrella（雨傘）、kettle（水壺）、cookie（餅乾）都不是氣候行動要保護的對象。
save our planet「拯救我們的地球」。pillow（枕頭）、towel（毛巾）、sock（襪子）都不是世界領袖要拯救的對象。
received honorary MBEs「獲頒榮譽大英帝國員佐勳章」，receive 表示「收到、獲得」。cried（哭）、slept（睡覺）、coughed（咳嗽）都不能接勳章當受詞。
do her part for the earth「為地球盡一份心力」。button（鈕扣）、bottle（瓶子）、scarf（圍巾）都不合句意。

gloss: 榮譽大英帝國員佐勳章
passages.zh: BLACKPINK 是全世界最受歡迎的女團之一。2021 年 2 月，四位成員 Jisoo、Jennie、Rosé 和 Lisa 被任命為 COP26 的倡議代言人。COP26 是聯合國討論氣候變遷的大型會議，那年 11 月在蘇格蘭格拉斯哥舉行。身為代言人，BLACKPINK 拍了影片，請粉絲認識氣候變遷並採取行動保護環境。會議期間，她們也送出一段影片訊息，請世界各國領袖盡快行動，拯救我們的地球。世界各地很多粉絲都在網路上分享這些影片。2023 年 11 月，成員們在倫敦獲得英王查爾斯三世頒發的榮譽大英帝國員佐勳章，表揚她們擔任 COP26 代言人的貢獻。我朋友艾咪是 BLACKPINK 的忠實粉絲，看了她們的氣候影片後，她開始離開房間時隨手關燈。她說她想和最喜歡的團體一樣，為地球盡一份心力。

passages.title: Jin 的月亮和太空人
passages.text: Jin of BTS seems to love space. In 2020, he sang a solo song called "Moon" on the album Map of the Soul: 7. In the song, Jin compares himself to the {1}, which always goes around the {2}. In his song, the earth is his fans, ARMY, so he will always stay close to them. Then, on October 28, 2022, Jin released his first solo single, "The Astronaut." He wrote it with the British band Coldplay. On the same day, he sang it live for the first time at Coldplay's concert in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Many fans saw the song as a {3} from Jin, because he {4} the military that December. While he was away, fans all over the {5} kept playing his songs. When Jin came back in June 2024, my cousin cried with joy. She said the moon had finally come home.

blanks.why: compares himself to the moon「把自己比喻成月亮」，歌名就是 "Moon"。pillow（枕頭）、wallet（皮夾）、kettle（水壺）不會「繞著地球轉」。
goes around the earth「繞著地球轉」，月亮是地球的衛星。sock（襪子）、bottle（瓶子）、towel（毛巾）都不是月亮繞行的對象。
a gift from Jin「Jin 送給粉絲的禮物」。cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）、headache（頭痛）都不會讓粉絲「看成是 Jin 給的」好東西。
joined the military「入伍當兵」，join 表示「加入」。tasted（嚐）、boiled（煮沸）、smelled（聞）都不能接 the military。
fans all over the planet「全世界的粉絲」。cookie（餅乾）、button（鈕扣）、scarf（圍巾）上面不會有粉絲。

passages.zh: BTS 的 Jin 似乎很喜歡太空。2020 年，他在專輯《Map of the Soul: 7》裡唱了一首個人歌曲〈Moon〉。在歌裡，Jin 把自己比喻成總是繞著地球轉的月亮，而地球就是他的粉絲 ARMY，所以他會一直待在他們身邊。後來在 2022 年 10 月 28 日，Jin 發行了第一張個人單曲〈The Astronaut〉，這首歌是他和英國的酷玩樂團一起寫的。同一天，他在酷玩樂團於阿根廷布宜諾斯艾利斯的演唱會上首次現場演唱這首歌。很多粉絲把這首歌看成 Jin 送的禮物，因為他那年 12 月就入伍了。他不在的時候，全世界的粉絲一直播放他的歌。2024 年 6 月 Jin 退伍回來時，我表姊開心得哭了。她說月亮終於回家了。

passages.title: 太陽和月亮組成的 MAMAMOO+
passages.text: MAMAMOO is a Korean girl {1} that debuted in 2014. It has four {2}: Solar, Moonbyul, Wheein, and Hwasa. The group is famous for strong live singing. In 2022, Solar and Moonbyul formed a unit called MAMAMOO+. When I first learned their names, I thought they were a perfect match. Solar's stage name makes people think of the sun. Moonbyul's family name is Moon, and "byul" means "star" in Korean. So the unit has the sun, the {3}, and a star! I told my science teacher about it. She laughed and said, "In real life, the sun is a star, and the earth is a {4}. The moon goes around the {5}, not around the sun!" I said that was fine with me. On stage, Solar and Moonbyul shine together, and that is the only science I need.

blanks.why: a Korean girl group「韓國女子團體」。cough（咳嗽）、spoon（湯匙）、fever（發燒）都不能和 girl 組成「出道」的對象。
four members「四位成員」，後面列出四個人名。coughs、fevers、spoons 都不能用人名來列舉。
the sun, the moon, and a star「太陽、月亮和星星」，Moonbyul 的姓 Moon 讓人聯想到月亮。ladder（梯子）、carpet（地毯）、tissue（面紙）和太陽、星星並列不合理。
the earth is a planet「地球是一顆行星」，老師在說明天體的分類：太陽是恆星、地球是行星。blanket（毛毯）、button（鈕扣）、kettle（水壺）都不能用來說明地球是什麼。
The moon goes around the earth「月亮繞著地球轉」，和 not the sun 對照。wallet（皮夾）、bottle（瓶子）、sock（襪子）都不是月亮繞行的對象。

passages.zh: MAMAMOO 是 2014 年出道的韓國女子團體，有四位成員：Solar、Moonbyul、Wheein 和 Hwasa，以強大的現場演唱實力聞名。2022 年，Solar 和 Moonbyul 組成了小分隊 MAMAMOO+。我第一次知道她們的名字時，覺得她們真是絕配：Solar 這個藝名讓人想到太陽；Moonbyul 姓 Moon（文），而 byul 在韓文裡是「星星」的意思。所以這個小分隊有太陽、月亮，還有一顆星星！我把這件事告訴自然老師，她笑著說：「在現實中，太陽是一顆恆星，地球是一顆行星。月亮是繞著地球轉，不是繞著太陽轉！」我說沒關係，在舞台上 Solar 和 Moonbyul 一起閃閃發光，這就是我唯一需要的科學。

passages.title: K-pop 粉絲一起救地球
passages.text: K-pop is {1} all over the world, and its fans are famous for working together. Some fans use this power to help the {2}. In 2021, a group of K-pop fans started Kpop4Planet, an online group for fans who care about climate change. One of the people who started it is Nurul Sarifah from Indonesia. The group noticed that many fans buy lots of copies of the same album to get different photo cards. Many of these albums are never played, and the plastic becomes {3}. So the group asked music companies to use less plastic and to offer more digital albums. They have also asked big companies to use clean energy instead of coal, which causes air {4}. Their idea is simple: if our {5} is not healthy, there will be no K-pop to enjoy. After I read about them, I decided to buy only one copy of my favorite group's new album.

blanks.why: popular all over the world「全世界都很受歡迎」。sore（痠痛的）、dizzy（頭暈的）、thirsty（口渴的）都不能形容一種音樂。
help the environment「幫助環境」，下文說這個團體關心氣候變遷。pumpkin（南瓜）、candle（蠟燭）、eraser（橡皮擦）都不是粉絲要幫助的對象。
the plastic becomes waste「塑膠變成廢棄物」。joy（喜悅）、talent（天分）、fault（過錯）都不是塑膠會變成的東西。
coal, which causes air pollution「燒煤會造成空氣汙染」。pillow（枕頭）、towel（毛巾）、bottle（瓶子）都不能和 air 組成燒煤的後果。
if our planet is not healthy「如果我們的地球不健康」。sock（襪子）、wallet（皮夾）、scarf（圍巾）不健康，和「沒有 K-pop 可聽」沒有關係。

passages.zh: K-pop 在全世界都很受歡迎，而它的粉絲以團結合作出名。有些粉絲用這股力量來幫助環境。2021 年，一群 K-pop 粉絲成立了 Kpop4Planet，這是一個給關心氣候變遷的粉絲參加的線上團體，創辦人之一是來自印尼的努魯‧莎莉法。這個團體注意到，很多粉絲為了收集不同的小卡，會買好幾張同一張專輯。這些專輯很多從來沒被播放過，塑膠就變成了廢棄物。所以他們請唱片公司少用塑膠，並推出更多數位專輯。他們也請大企業改用乾淨能源，不要用會造成空氣汙染的煤。他們的想法很簡單：如果我們的地球不健康，就沒有 K-pop 可以享受了。讀到他們的故事後，我決定最喜歡的團體出新專輯時，我只買一張。

passages.title: 老師的太空冷笑話
passages.text: Our science teacher, Ms. Lin, loves bad jokes, and her {1} topic is space. Last Friday, she asked us, "How do you get ready for a party in space?" Nobody knew the answer. "You {2}!" she said. It sounds like "You plan it." We all groaned. Then she asked, "What did the {3} say to the other planets?" She answered, "You guys have no life!" Some of us laughed, because the earth is the only planet we know of with living things on it. Her last joke was, "How does the {4} cut its hair?" The answer was, "Eclipse it!" It sounds like "He clips it." Before the bell rang, she told us that our {5} was to write our own space joke. I am still thinking about mine. Maybe I will ask why the sun didn't go to university. Because it already had millions of degrees!

blanks.why: her favorite topic「她最喜歡的話題」。dizzy（頭暈的）、sore（痠痛的）、thirsty（口渴的）都不能形容話題。
You planet!「你規劃它！」planet 唸起來像 plan it（計畫它），這就是笑話的梗。pillow、kettle、sock 唸起來都不像 plan it，也不好笑。
What did the earth say to the other planets「地球對其他行星說了什麼」，後面說地球是唯一有生命的行星。spoon（湯匙）、blanket（毛毯）、towel（毛巾）不是行星，不能說 the other planets。
How does the moon cut its hair「月亮怎麼剪頭髮」，答案 Eclipse it（日月食）唸起來像 He clips it（他剪它）。wallet（皮夾）、bottle（瓶子）、carpet（地毯）都和 eclipse 無關，笑話就不成立。
our homework was to write…「我們的作業是寫……」。fever（發燒）、cough（咳嗽）、headache（頭痛）都不會是老師出的「要寫一個笑話」的事。

passages.zh: 我們的自然老師林老師很愛講冷笑話，她最喜歡的話題是太空。上星期五，她問我們：「在太空要怎麼準備派對？」沒有人知道答案。「You planet！」她說。這聽起來像「你把它規劃好（plan it）」。我們全都唉了一聲。接著她問：「地球對其他行星說了什麼？」她回答：「你們都沒有生命（沒有生活）！」有些人笑了，因為地球是我們目前所知唯一有生物的行星。她最後一個笑話是：「月亮怎麼剪頭髮？」答案是：「Eclipse it！」聽起來像「他把它剪一剪（He clips it）」。下課鐘響前，她說我們的作業是自己寫一個太空笑話。我還在想要寫什麼，也許我會問太陽為什麼沒去讀大學——因為它早就有好幾百萬度（學位）了！

passages.title: 月球上的新餐廳
passages.text: At dinner last night, my brother told me a joke. "Did you hear about the new restaurant on the {1}? The food is great, but there's no atmosphere." I didn't get it at first, so he {2} it to me. The moon has almost no air around it, unlike the {3}. The air around a planet is called its atmosphere. But "atmosphere" can also mean the feeling of a place, like when a restaurant is warm and friendly. So the joke means the restaurant is a bit boring! Then Dad joined in. "What kind of music do {4} like?" he asked. "Nep-tunes!" Mom rolled her eyes, but she smiled. I said I would love to eat at the moon restaurant someday. My brother said, "You can't even {5} a bubble tea every day. How can you pay for a trip to the moon?" Everyone laughed, even me.

blanks.why: the new restaurant on the moon「月球上的新餐廳」，月球沒有大氣，才有 no atmosphere 的笑點。sofa（沙發）、tissue（面紙）、ladder（梯子）上面不會開餐廳。
explained it to me「解釋給我聽」，explain + 事 + to + 人。swam（游泳）、slept（睡覺）不能接受詞，boiled it to me（把它煮給我）意思不通。
unlike the earth「和地球不一樣」，地球有大氣層，月球幾乎沒有。pillow（枕頭）、cookie（餅乾）、button（鈕扣）本來就不是有「大氣」的天體，不能拿來對比。
What kind of music do planets like「行星喜歡哪種音樂」，答案 Nep-tunes 是 Neptune（海王星）和 tunes（曲子）的雙關。spoons、socks、kettles 和海王星無關，笑話就不成立。
can't even afford a bubble tea「連一杯珍奶都買不起」，afford 表示「負擔得起」，下一句說 pay for a trip。explore（探索）、imagine（想像）、decorate（裝飾）都和「付錢」無關，接 every day 和後面的 pay for 也接不上。

passages.zh: 昨天晚餐時，我哥哥跟我講了一個笑話：「你聽說月球上新開的餐廳了嗎？東西很好吃，可是沒有 atmosphere。」我一開始聽不懂，所以他解釋給我聽：月球和地球不一樣，周圍幾乎沒有空氣，而行星周圍的空氣叫做大氣層（atmosphere）。但 atmosphere 也可以指一個地方的氣氛，像是一家溫暖友善的餐廳。所以這個笑話是說那家餐廳有點無聊！接著爸爸也加入：「行星喜歡哪一種音樂？」他問。「Nep-tunes（海王星曲）！」媽媽翻了個白眼，但還是笑了。我說總有一天我想去月球餐廳吃飯。哥哥說：「你連每天一杯珍奶都買不起，怎麼付得起去月球的旅費？」大家都笑了，連我也是。
